title: Basic internet access is expanding while quality, affordability, skills, and location continue to stratify meaningful digital participation
source_unit: ITU, Measuring digital development: Facts and Figures 2025
geography: Global, with income-group, gender, age, and urban-rural comparisons

observations.period: 2025 global connectivity estimates; report released 17 November 2025

denominator.unit: global population and internet-use estimate frame

online_population.unit: approximately people using the Internet in 2025; about three-quarters of world population

annual_online_growth.unit: more people online in 2025 than in 2024, approximately

observations.method: ITU annual global, regional, and income-group estimates for internet use and related connectivity indicators, with revised prior-year estimates based on the latest available data.
observations.uncertainty: These are modeled and compiled population estimates, not a single respondent panel. Revisions, missing country data, definitions of use, and population denominators affect comparability; being online does not establish quality, safety, affordability, or meaningful use.
observations.subgroup: People by country income group, gender, age, geography, device access, service quality, affordability, and digital skill level.
observations.counterinterpretation: Rapid expansion can coexist with meaningful improvements for newly connected populations; remaining offline or low-intensity use does not by itself identify preference, harm, or exclusion caused by a specific provider or policy.

denominator.unit: global population, network-coverage, mobile-broadband, and ICT-price comparison frame

five_g_population_coverage.unit: percent of world population covered by 5G networks in 2025

five_g_high_income_coverage.unit: percent of people in high-income countries with 5G access

five_g_low_income_coverage.unit: percent of people in low-income countries with 5G access

unaffordable_lmic_baskets.unit: approximately percent of low- and middle-income countries where a data-only mobile-broadband basket remains unaffordable

observations.method: ITU comparison of mobile-network coverage, subscriptions, data use, and ICT affordability across global income groups and countries.
observations.uncertainty: Coverage is not equivalent to service availability, subscription, device ownership, reliability, or ability to pay. The affordability threshold and basket vary by methodology and do not measure household trade-offs or actual use.
observations.subgroup: High- and low-income countries, low- and middle-income countries, rural and urban populations, and users with different devices and service plans.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower 5G coverage can reflect different technology paths or later deployment rather than absolute exclusion; 4G and 3G coverage may still support important use, though they may not support emerging data-intensive services equally.

denominator.unit: global internet-use population comparison by income, gender, location, and age

high_income_online.unit: percent of people in high-income countries using the Internet

low_income_online.unit: percent of people in low-income countries using the Internet

men_online.unit: percent of men using the Internet

women_online.unit: percent of women using the Internet

urban_online.unit: percent of people in urban areas using the Internet

rural_online.unit: percent of people in rural areas using the Internet

observations.method: ITU global, regional, and income-group estimates with subgroup comparisons for economic development, gender, age, and urban-rural location.
observations.uncertainty: These descriptive gaps do not isolate infrastructure, price, education, device, safety, language, social norms, or individual choice as causes. Group averages conceal within-country and within-group variation.
observations.subgroup: People by income group, gender, urban-rural location, age, education, and region; 96% of those offline are reported to live in low- and middle-income countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: The gaps may narrow as infrastructure, prices, devices, skills, and social conditions change; access parity alone would still not prove equal quality, safety, autonomy, or benefit from digital participation.

related_sources.claim: ITU companion Global Connectivity Report 2025 frames universal and meaningful connectivity around quality, availability, affordability, devices, skills, and security.
ITU chapter on digital skills and opportunities.

boundary: This record adds a global connectivity-to-digital-participation and unequal-optionality route. It is not respondent-level data, does not estimate individual online behavior or welfare, and does not establish that connectivity caused cultural, political, consumer, work, or trust outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official ITU Facts and Figures page and press release were retrieved; online population, offline population, 5G coverage, affordability, income, gender, and urban-rural figures were cross-checked against official ITU materials. The hash is a source-URL fingerprint because the ITU PDF host was not required for the claims used here.
